title: RNA sequencing reveals that TSP-4/STAT3 signaling reduces odontoblast apoptosis.
abstract: Bacteria from dental caries and their toxic products can induce apoptosis of odontoblasts via sustained and intense stimulation. In this study, we profiled the transcriptomes of healthy and carious human odontoblastic layer and investigated the role of thrombospondin-4 (TSP-4) in reducing odontoblast apoptosis under inflammatory conditions. In the human clinical model, odontoblastic layers isolated from healthy and carious teeth were subjected to RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq). Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses were performed to investigate gene expression profiles. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were validated with RT-qPCR. Further, western blot and immunofluorescence were used to detect TSP-4 expression. The mouse caries model was used to confirm TSP-4 expression in vivo. In the human odontoblastic-like cells (hOBLCs) model, cells were treated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS), small interfering RNA (siRNA) targeting TSP-4, recombinant human TSP-4 (rhTSP-4), Stattic, and siRNA targeting signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). TSP-4 and caspase-3 expression and STAT3 phosphorylation were assessed using western blot. Apoptosis was evaluated by flow cytometry analysis. In the human clinical model, RNA-seq results identified 779 DEGs. GO and KEGG analyses showed that DEGs were enriched in the extracellular matrix organization. TSP-4 expression was increased in carious human dental pulp and in mouse carious dental pulp. In the hOBLCs model, LPS treatment increased TSP-4 expression. TSP-4 knockdown suppressed STAT3 phosphorylation and promoted apoptosis, while rhTSP-4 treatment increased STAT3 phosphorylation and decreased apoptosis, which was abolished by Stattic or siSTAT3. Gene expression profiles of the odontoblastic layer in healthy and carious human teeth were identified. TSP-4 was found to regulate apoptosis in hOBLCs via STAT3 signaling. This study may deepen our understanding of dental pulp inflammation and offer a potential therapeutic target for preventing odontoblast apoptosis and subsequent damage during caries progression.
authors: Ruoxia Jiang; Wanhua Li; Weiwei Qiao; Liuyan Meng
